questions.q: A building is located such that 40% of its total floor area is in a Highly Fire Restrictive Zone and 60% is in a Non-Fire Restricted Zone. How is the building classified?
o: The Architect chooses which zone to follow
It is split and follows two different rules
questions.n: Section 502 states that if more than 1/3 (33.3%) of the area is in a more restrictive zone, the entire building must comply with that zone.

questions.q: Which specific entity has the power to enact ordinances designating fire zones within a local jurisdiction?
o: The Legislative Body of the LGU
The Department of Public Works and Highways
questions.n: Section 507 mandates that the local legislative body (like the Sanggunian) enacts these ordinances.

questions.q: In 'Highly Fire Restrictive Zones', what is the minimum fire-resistive requirement for construction materials used throughout the building?
o: No less than three to four-hour
questions.n: Section 507 defines these zones as requiring 3 to 4-hour fire-resistive materials throughout.

questions.q: If a pre-fabricated building is dismantled and re-assembled in a new fire zone, which requirements must it follow?
o: No requirements, as it is a temporary structure
Only the plumbing and electrical codes
All requirements for buildings in the new fire zone
The requirements of its original location
questions.n: Section 503.2 specifically applies the compliance rule to moved, dismantled, and re-assembled structures.

questions.q: Under Section 505, how is the distance between a building and an adjoining street or alley measured?
o: From the building to the opposite property line
From the building to the nearest sidewalk
At right angles to the center line of the street
questions.n: Section 505 states the center line may be considered an adjacent property line, measured at right angles.

questions.q: What is required for 'temporary buildings' like reviewing stands or construction sheds to be erected in fire zones?
o: No permit is needed if removed in 30 days
A verbal agreement with the owner
A special permit from the Building Official
questions.n: Section 504.1 requires a special permit for temporary structures like stands and construction sheds.

questions.q: In which zone are dwellings made of indigenous materials like bamboo, sawali, and nipa typically permitted?
questions.n: Section 507 defines these as rural/countryside areas where indigenous materials are permitted.

questions.q: Can an existing building in a fire zone that does NOT comply with new requirements be enlarged?
o: No, it shall not be enlarged
Yes, if the addition is fire-proof
Yes, but only by 10% of floor area
questions.n: Section 506.1 states that non-compliant existing buildings shall not hereafter be enlarged.

questions.q: In a 'Fire Restrictive Zone', exterior walls are generally required to have at least how many hours of fire resistivity?
questions.n: Section 507 describes Fire Restrictive Zones as requiring at least two-hour fire resistivity for exterior walls.

questions.q: The designation of fire zones is based on which of the following parameters?
o: Use/occupancy, type of construction, and fire resistance
questions.n: Section 501 defines fire zones based on these three core safety parameters.

questions.q: Which specific zone allows for the construction of buildings using indigenous materials like bamboo and nipa without mandatory fire-resistivity measures?
questions.n: Section 507 describes these as rural or sparsely constructed areas where indigenous materials and Types I and II construction are permitted.

questions.q: According to Section 502, if only 20% of a building's total floor area falls into a 'more restrictive' fire zone, which zone's rules does the building follow?
o: The zone where the main entrance is located
questions.n: Since 20% is less than the one-third threshold mentioned in Section 502, the building is not forced into the more restrictive classification.

questions.q: What is the minimum fire-resistivity requirement for the exterior walls of buildings located in a 'Fire Restrictive Zone'?
questions.n: Section 507 specifies that Fire Restrictive Zones require exterior walls of at least two-hour fire resistivity.

questions.q: To erect temporary structures like construction sheds or reviewing stands in a fire zone, whose permission is required?
o: Special permit from the Building Official
questions.n: Section 504.1 states these temporary structures may be erected by special permit from the Building Official.

questions.q: What happens to a pre-engineered building that is dismantled and re-assembled in a 'Highly Fire Restrictive Zone'?
o: It only needs to comply if it is enlarged.
It must comply with all requirements of the new zone.
It keeps its original fire rating.
It is exempt as it was previously approved.
questions.n: Section 503 states any building moved or re-assembled must comply with the requirements of the zone it moves into.

questions.q: Under Section 505, the center line of an adjoining street or alley may be considered as what?
questions.n: Section 505 explicitly states the center line may be considered an adjacent property line for measurement purposes.

questions.q: In Highly Fire Restrictive Zones, buildings must use construction assemblies with no less than ________ fire-resistive materials throughout.
questions.n: Section 507 defines Highly Fire Restrictive Zones as requiring 3 to 4-hour fire-resistive construction throughout.

questions.q: True or False: An existing building that does not comply with its current fire zone's requirements can be enlarged as long as the new addition is compliant.
questions.n: Section 506.1 states that non-compliant existing buildings shall not hereafter be enlarged.

questions.q: Who is responsible for enacting the ordinances that actually designate which areas of a city belong to which fire zone?
o: The Legislative Body of the LGU
questions.n: Section 507 states that the legislative body (like the City Council) enacts the ordinances for designating zones.

questions.q: Fire zones are primarily defined and permitted based on their use/occupancy, resistance to fire, and what other factor?
questions.n: Section 501 defines fire zones based on use, resistance to fire, and the type of construction (e.g., Types I-V).

questions.q: In which specific zone would you find buildings constructed of indigenous materials such as sawali, nipa, and bamboo?
questions.n: Section 507 describes these areas as typically rural where dwellings built of indigenous materials are permitted.

questions.q: According to Section 505, how is the distance measured when the center line of an adjoining street is considered an adjacent property line?
o: From the building to the sidewalk edge
At right angles to the street or alley
questions.n: Section 505 explicitly states that distances shall be measured at right angles to the street or alley.

questions.q: What is the mandatory fire-resistivity requirement for construction materials used throughout 'Highly Fire Restrictive Zones'?
o: No less than three to four-hour
questions.n: Section 507 defines Highly Fire Restrictive Zones as requiring three to four-hour fire-resistive construction materials throughout.

questions.q: For a building spanning two zones, what is the 'threshold' percentage that forces the entire building to follow the more restrictive zone's rules?
questions.n: Section 502 states that if more than one third of the total floor area is in the more restrictive zone, that zone's rules apply.

questions.q: When a pre-fabricated building is moved and re-assembled in a different fire zone, it must:
o: Comply with all requirements of the new fire zone
Only comply if it is a permanent structure
questions.n: Section 503.2 specifically requires moved or re-assembled structures to follow the rules of their current zone.

questions.q: Under Section 504, who has the authority to issue 'special permits' for temporary structures like construction sheds in fire zones?
o: The Legislative Body of the LGU
questions.n: Section 504.1 states that these structures may be erected by special permit from the Building Official.

questions.q: Fire Restrictive Zones typically require exterior walls to have at least how many hours of fire resistivity?
questions.n: Section 507 specifies exterior walls must have at least two-hour fire resistivity in Fire Restrictive Zones.

questions.q: What is the rule regarding the enlargement of existing buildings in fire zones that do not comply with the zone's new requirements?
o: They can be enlarged with a permit from the LGU.
They can be enlarged up to 50% of the area.
They shall not hereafter be enlarged.
They can be enlarged if they use steel frames.
questions.n: Section 506.1 explicitly prohibits the enlargement of existing non-compliant buildings in fire zones.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three primary factors used to define a fire zone according to Section 501?
questions.n: Aesthetics like building color have no impact on fire zone designation or safety standards.

questions.q: True or False: The 'Fire Restrictive Zones' are usually located in suburban areas.
questions.n: Section 507 notes that these zones are usually found in suburban locations where one-hour resistivity throughout is permitted.
